title: ADR-0018 — Bind prepublication evidence to tree content, not commit identity
description: Compare prepublication evidence against the git tree hash of candidate content, and run ci:prepublish as a real pre-merge required check, so the gate can be satisfied by a real merge.
searchText: adr-0018 — bind prepublication evidence to tree content, not commit identity compare prepublication evidence against the git tree hash of candidate content, and run ci:prepublish as a real pre-merge required check, so the gate can be satisfied by a real merge. decisions adr approved cicd security phase-1-5 prepublication evidence is now compared by git tree content, not commit sha identity, resolving 2026 08 10. context the completion audit's authoritative prepublication check gate compares prepublication evidence (produced by npm run ci:prepublish ) against the exact commit sha of the candidate under review, via validatepublicationcandidate 's hard fail check that evidence.candidatesha === candidatesha . that equality can never survive a real merge into main . github always server generates a new commit sha when a pull request is merged — whether by merge commit, squash, or rebase — even when the merged file content is byte identical to the reviewed branch tip. so evidence generated pre merge, bound to the pre merge commit sha, is structurally guaranteed to fail comparison against the post merge main head sha, regardless of how sound the underlying gates were. the gate was unsatisfiable by design, not by a bug in any individual gate. compounding this, evidence/publication readiness.json and evidence/publication evidence.json are local only, gitignored artifacts. ci:prepublish had never run as a required pre merge ci check, so even setting aside the sha equality problem, no ci produced evidence for a candidate existed to compare against in the first place. decision drivers the gate must be satisfiable by a normal, real github merge into main , not only by an artificial same sha condition that a merge can never produce; the gate must not become materially weaker in what it guarantees — it must still catch a case where the actual reviewed file content differs from what is being published; the fix should reuse an existing, precedented pattern in this codebase rather than invent a new content binding mechanism; evidence must actually be produced pre merge, by ci, not only by a local developer run, or the comparison has nothing authoritative to compare against. options considered this was an explicit decision made by the repository owner after investigation, not an autonomous engineering call. 1. rejected — relax the check to "candidate sha is an ancestor of the merged commit." this materially weakens the guarantee: it would also pass for a merge that manually resolved a conflict by hand editing content differently from what was reviewed, because a manually resolved merge commit has the reviewed commit as an ancestor regardless of what edits were made during conflict resolution. an ancestor relationship proves lineage, not that the published content matches what was evaluated. rejected because it does not survive the exact failure mode it would need to catch. 2. adopted, in combination — add a real, required ci check that runs ci:prepublish on the pull request itself, pre merge, uploading the evidence as a build artifact. this produces authoritative, ci generated evidence to compare against, rather than relying on a locally generated file that was never ci verified. implemented in this decision as .github/workflows/pr prepublish.yml , job id prepublish . 3. adopted, in combination — compare the git tree hash of the candidate's file content instead of the commit sha. a git tree object id is a content hash of the full file tree; two commits with identical tree hashes have byte identical file content regardless of their distinct commit identities (author, timestamp, parent, message). this is strictly not weaker than commit sha equality for the purpose this gate serves (detecting content drift between what was evaluated and what is published) — it is exactly the same equality class (exact match), just applied to content instead of to unrelated to content commit metadata. this was empirically confirmed against this repository's own merge history: commit 1658a4a (the current main merge commit) and its pr branch tip parent 4905825 have identical tree 18ab7e93c923e309444d9aa69533c1437a317c52 , confirming that a real, zero drift merge in this repository does produce identical tree content across distinct commit shas — the exact case this gate needs to tolerate. this option is also precedented by the diffsha256 content binding pattern already used in src/modules/orchestration/publication/publication policy.ts , which compares diff content hashes rather than commit identity for a related purpose. decision adopt options 2 and 3 in combination. reject option 1. publicationreadinessevidenceschema gains a candidatetree field (same 40 hex char shape as candidatesha , produced by git rev parse head^{tree} ). validatepublicationcandidate now takes (input, candidatesha, candidatetree) and hard fails when evidence.candidatetree !== candidatetree , rather than when evidence.candidatesha !== candidatesha . candidatesha remains in the schema and in the failure reason message for traceability, but it is no longer the field being compared for equality. scripts/ci/prepublish.mjs computes and records candidatetree alongside candidatesha when generating evidence. scripts/ci/authorize publication.mjs and scripts/agents/audit phase 1.5.mjs both resolve the candidate's tree hash and pass it through to validatepublicationcandidate . a new workflow, .github/workflows/pr prepublish.yml , runs npm run ci:prepublish base origin/main on every pull request targeting main and uploads evidence/publication readiness.json and evidence/publication evidence.json as a build artifact, so ci — not only a local developer run — produces authoritative, checkable prepublication evidence for a candidate before merge. implementation status this decision covers code, tests, the new workflow, and documentation only. the following is explicit follow up work, not done in this change: adding the prepublish job's check context to the main branch protection ruleset's required status checks ; enabling strict required status checks policy ("require branches to be up to date before merging") for that ruleset. both require a live github api mutation against the repository's ruleset, which is out of scope for this change and gated on a separate, later approval (see risks below). positive consequences authoritative prepublication check becomes satisfiable by a real github merge, closing a structurally unsatisfiable gate without weakening what it detects; prepublication evidence is now produced by ci on the pull request itself, not only by an uncommitted local file, giving the gate something authoritative to compare against; the fix reuses this repository's existing content hash binding pattern ( diffsha256 in publication policy.ts ) rather than introducing a new mechanism; the rejected "ancestor of" relaxation is explicitly documented as rejected, so it is not silently reintroduced later. negative consequences one more required field ( candidatetree ) must be kept in sync everywhere candidatesha is computed; the new pr prepublish.yml workflow adds ci runtime cost to every qualifying pull request; until the ruleset is updated (follow up work below), prepublish running in ci does not yet block a merge — it currently only produces evidence, it does not yet gate it at the github level. risks residual risk this change does not yet close: tree hash comparison against a pull request's own head can false pass content that has silently drifted from main , or false fail on unrelated main drift, unless github's strict required status checks policy ("require branches up to date before merging") is also enabled for the ruleset that requires the prepublish context. that live ruleset mutation is explicitly out of scope for this change and requires a separate live test then approval step: open a throwaway pull request, cause real drift on main , confirm the new prepublish check fails on a stale tree, sync the branch, confirm it then passes — only after that live verification should the ruleset be flipped via a gh api mutation, and only with separate approval. a tree hash comparison, like a sha comparison, only detects file content drift; it cannot detect a compromised ci runner producing an evidence file for content it did not actually evaluate — this remains an assumed trust boundary of the existing evidence model, unchanged by this decision. follow up work 1. open a throwaway pull request, cause real main drift while it is open, and confirm the new prepublish check fails against the stale candidate tree. 2. sync that pull request's branch and confirm prepublish then passes. 3. only after that live verification, and with separate approval, mutate the branch protection ruleset: add prepublish to required status checks and set strict required status checks policy to true . 4. re run npm run phase15:audit once the ruleset changes land, to confirm the agent platform required check style gate treatment extends correctly to prepublish . supersedes or superseded by new decision; superseded by: none. it amends the prepublication evidence mechanism introduced under adr 0017's platform completion scope without superseding adr 0017's overall phase boundary. source references title: ADR-0023 — Define provider-neutral execution budget semantics
description: Proposes canonical hard execution-budget lineage semantics for provider model calls and cumulative output tokens across direct providers, harnesses, and future adapters.
searchText: adr-0023 — define provider-neutral execution budget semantics proposes canonical hard execution-budget lineage semantics for provider model calls and cumulative output tokens across direct providers, harnesses, and future adapters. decisions adr under-review phase-1-5 provider-adapter execution-budget least-privilege proposal only: define provider neutral hard execution budgets shared by one authorized execution lineage. this proposal changes no runtime, approves no adapter, and grants no routing, provider, deployment, release, or merge authority. context beacon's phase 1.5 role contracts and model policy declare maxturns , maxcontexttokens , and maxoutputtokens . the live execution boundary copies maxturns and maxoutputtokens into providerexecutionrequest , passes the request to a provideradapter , and records providerrun.turns , providerrun.retrycount , and normalized output token usage afterward. those fields are measurable looking but do not currently share a binding provider neutral meaning. maxturns originated in claude subagent frontmatter as a cap on agentic turns. the phase 1.5 provider work then copied the same name into the shared adapter request without defining what one turn means for a direct http request, a cli harness, a tool loop, or a retry. maxoutputtokens is forwarded to direct provider request fields, but no accepted architecture says whether it is a per call allowance or a cumulative allowance for the authorized execution. this ambiguity became blocking while draft adr 0022 and pr 76 evaluated a deterministic opencode isolation profile for pr 0.6. opencode specific architecture must not invent stronger or weaker meanings than claude, codex, and future adapters receive from the shared execution contract. the first under review revision of this adr proposed cumulative budgets owned by one providerexecutionrequest . independent technical review found that request ownership would allow a retry, subagent, fallback, handoff, provider switch, or separately constructed request to begin with fresh counters. that would defeat a cumulative execution contract. this corrected proposal makes an authorized execution lineage, not a javascript or typescript request object, the lifetime and owner of the budget. current main was inspected at b5cde2c9c472e89db02f9fb4009395a5901a2838 . its tree matches the successful candidate bound prepublication evidence from pr 75, and a fresh npm run phase15:audit with that exact tree evidence returned complete frozen . this proposal therefore treats existing phase 1.5 behavior as frozen reality to be documented honestly, not silently rewritten. problem a policy limit, authoritative enforcement state, and telemetry value are different contracts: post execution telemetry cannot prevent an unauthorized model call or undo generated tokens. prompt instructions, provider native settings with advisory semantics, wall clock timeouts, and an observed count after completion are not hard execution budget enforcement. without one canonical meaning and one stable budget lifetime, adapters can accept equivalent work while interpreting or resetting limits differently. that makes provider replacement unsafe, prevents conformance tests from proving bounded execution, and invites a third party harness, retry loop, or fallback path to multiply cost or authority behind fields that appear bounded. evidence the review covered accepted adr 0007, adr 0008, adr 0010, adr 0012, adr 0014, adr 0015, adr 0017, adr 0019, adr 0020, adr 0021, draft adr 0022 in pr 76, phase 1.5 architecture and security pages, the phase 1.6 v6.5.1 execution constitution, pr 0b event identity and replay semantics, agent and model policies, runtime/domain schemas, direct and cli transports, live execution scripts, provider tests, live eval contracts, telemetry schemas, and repository history for both fields. the introducing history supplies no provider neutral definition. contract validation proves only that role values are positive integers, that maxoutputtokens is lower than maxcontexttokens , and that the role manifest, model policy, and claude agent frontmatter do not drift. the budget bounds catalog label does not execute a provider or prove a runtime stop. current official provider documentation confirms that anthropic max tokens is an absolute maximum for one messages api generation and openai max output tokens is an upper bound for one responses api response that includes visible and reasoning tokens. those are useful per call enforcement mechanisms. they do not, by themselves, define an aggregate budget across multiple calls, retries, fallbacks, or provider transitions in one authorized execution. existing implementation reality contract / field declared meaning actual enforcement claude codex harness / opencode tests gap role limits.maxturns ; providerexecutionrequest.maxturns positive bounded agent value; no provider neutral unit is defined. passed through executeliveworkunit ; not read by current adapters or workflow guards. one transport invocation by current adapter structure; request value is ignored. one adapter transport invocation, but the cli can perform opaque internal work; request value is ignored. released opencode agent.steps is guidance/tool suppression, not a proven hard stop. positivity and manifest/frontmatter drift only. no canonical model call field, stable budget lineage, pre call ledger, retry rule, or hard denial of call n+1. role limits.maxoutputtokens ; providerexecutionrequest.maxoutputtokens positive output budget lower than the context budget; per call versus aggregate is undefined. forwarded to provider payloads; no aggregate accounting or request to usage comparison. forwarded as max tokens for one messages api request. forwarded as max output tokens ; the http path sends it, while codexclitransport drops it. current opencode controls cap individual model responses, not aggregate subprocess output. valid values and response normalization; no adversarial cumulative budget proof. a multi call or multi request execution can multiply the apparent budget unless a trusted ledger reserves the shared remaining output before every generation branch. providerrun.turns ; agentrun.execution.turns non negative observed telemetry. buildproviderresult currently writes 1 ; agentrun copies it. always reported as 1 by the shared builder. always reported as 1 , including the opaque cli path. draft normalizers can observe events but cannot infer calls that begin without a pre call barrier. schema shape and fixture values only. observed telemetry is not tied to the requested ceiling and may undercount opaque or failed calls. providerrun.usage.outputtokens normalized observed provider output; nullable in the general schema. parsed after execution; no enforcement comparison. provider usage is normalized. http/cli usage is normalized when present; cli requires metrics but not the request cap. telemetry may be unavailable or per call only. normalization and consistency checks. observation after generation cannot serve as a hard pre/during execution ceiling or preserve conservative charges. providerrun.retrycount non negative observed retry telemetry. shared result builder writes 0 ; current workflow has no retry loop. 0 . 0 ; opaque cli behavior is not represented. not canonically related to model calls. schema shape and fixtures only. a retry may create another model call, while caller level retry can also construct a fresh request with no shared counter. the current state is therefore a pre existing architecture and contract defect: phase15 budget semantics gap phase 1.5 being complete frozen means the ambiguity must be resolved through an explicit human reviewed architecture decision and a separately reviewed bounded conformance change, not by editing current adapters inside this decision pr. decision drivers give every adapter the same measurable security unit regardless of provider vocabulary. bind cumulative limits to one authorized execution even when it crosses requests, retries, providers, or agent projections. deny the first model generation that would exceed either budget before it begins. prevent concurrent, batched, hedged, fan out, or opaque execution from multiplying capacity. count retries and implicit model calls conservatively and auditably. keep provider native hard controls usable without making their names authoritative. preserve the distinction between policy, enforcement ledger, and telemetry projection. fail closed when an adapter, transport, provider, or harness cannot prove control of every generation branch it may initiate. resolve the provider boundary maxturns naming collision without silently changing higher level agent policy. preserve phase 1.5 provider eligibility, routing, role, approval, and frozen runtime boundaries. options considered budget lifetime options option a — one providerexecutionrequest owns fresh budget state. rejected. retrying the call, constructing a fallback request, switching providers, creating a subagent request, or continuing through a handoff could restore the configured maxima and multiply one authorized execution's capacity. option b — one authorized execution budget lineage owns shared budget state. adopted. an immutable lineage identity connects every provider request and generation branch that consumes the same authorization. requests carry a reference to that lineage; they do not create or reset its ledger. option c — providerrun or agentrun telemetry owns the budget. rejected. those records are projections and may be absent on failure. post call telemetry cannot be the source of pre call enforcement truth, and one lineage may cross multiple providerruns or agentrun projections. model call limit naming options option a — a turn is whatever the provider calls a turn. rejected. provider steps, messages, responses, tool loops, and harness iterations are not equivalent, so the number would not be portable or reliably auditable. option b — maxmodelcalls is the canonical provider budget name; existing provider boundary maxturns is a legacy alias during migration. adopted. one model call means one model generation branch admitted on behalf of an execution budget lineage. the clear canonical name removes provider and agent loop ambiguity while permitting a bounded schema migration after acceptance. option c — keep maxturns as the canonical provider budget name. rejected. the role/agent layer already uses turn terminology for agentic workflow iterations. reusing it as the canonical name for provider generation calls invites a silent semantic collision. option d — a turn is one complete agent loop regardless of its underlying calls. rejected. one loop can hide an unbounded number of provider requests and therefore cannot guarantee that model call n+1 was denied before execution. output token limit options option a — maximum output tokens per model call. rejected as the canonical execution meaning. it permits a multi call adapter to generate up to maxoutputtokens × calls , multiplying the budget carried by one authorized execution. option b — maximum cumulative provider generated output tokens across one execution budget lineage. adopted. it remains bounded across retries, model re entry, internal calls, fallbacks, handoffs, provider switches, and multiple request objects. option c — add both maxoutputtokenspercall and maxtotaloutputtokens . deferred. a separate per call policy may become useful, but it is not required to enforce the cumulative ceiling: model call admission can derive a hard per call cap from the lineage's remaining total. adding two configured values now would broaden migration without evidence that callers need independent values. decision if approved, beacon adopts one provider neutral execution budget contract across claude, codex, opencode, and every future provider adapter: an authorized orchestration boundary creates an executionbudgetlineage with an immutable budgetlineageid , maxmodelcalls , and maxoutputtokens . the lineage's executionbudgetledger is the authoritative enforcement state. its remaining budgets are shared across every request and generation branch in that lineage. providerexecutionrequest carries execution information, configured constraints, and a reference to the lineage. constructing another request does not create or restore budget. maxmodelcalls is the canonical maximum number of model generation branches that may be initiated for the lineage. existing providerexecutionrequest.maxturns is legacy naming that must map exactly to maxmodelcalls during migration. maxoutputtokens is the hard cumulative ceiling on all provider generated output for the lineage. one atomic model call admission transaction reserves both one model call and one hard per call output allowance before any generation branch begins. every admitted branch receives a unique budgetreservationid and follows the reservation lifecycle defined below. both limits are policy controls enforced before or during execution by a trusted boundary. they are not prompts, hints, timeouts, or post call telemetry. an execution path must fail with a non retryable policy error before unbounded model execution when it cannot prove both ceilings, generation multiplicity, or required settlement behavior. only an authorized beacon orchestration boundary may create a new lineage. retry, fallback, handoff, provider switch, subagent creation, or arbitrary request construction does not authorize a reset. this proposal does not modify runtime or serialized schemas. if the repository owner accepts it, that acceptance supplies the missing semantic authority for a separate bounded phase 1.5 execution budget conformance hardening pr. it does not authorize routing, gateway, harness, provider, role budget, deployment, release, pr 1, or other feature expansion. formal definitions authorized execution and execution budget lineage an authorized execution is a beacon orchestration boundary at which policy explicitly grants bounded model execution capacity. a genuinely new top level workunit execution is an example. an explicitly authorized delegated child execution may also qualify when its bounded allocation and provenance are recorded. an executionbudgetlineage is the stable lifetime of that granted capacity. it is identified by an immutable budgetlineageid created by the authorized orchestration boundary and recorded in enforcement and audit state. the lineage, not any javascript or typescript object, owns the remaining model call and cumulative output token budgets. the same lineage continues across: provider transport retries; caller level retries of the same authorized execution; model re entry after local tool output; compaction, summarization, and title generation model calls; internal or model driven subagents; fallback agent model calls; ordinary provider fallback or provider switch; ordinary handoff that continues the same authorized execution; and separately constructed providerexecutionrequest values that continue that work. none of those operations may silently restore maxmodelcalls or maxoutputtokens . stable budget identity and new budget authority budgetlineageid must be stable and immutable for the lineage, included in authoritative ledger and audit evidence, and propagated to every trusted enforcement point that admits a call for that lineage. a new lineage may be created only by an authorized beacon orchestration boundary through all of these actions: 1. identify a distinct authorized execution boundary; 2. make an explicit bounded policy allocation decision; 3. create a new stable budget identity; 4. record the allocation and authority in durable audit evidence; and 5. preserve parent execution or budget provenance when applicable. a provideradapter , providertransport , retry loop, cli harness, opencode process, provider sdk, fallback path, or arbitrary constructor of providerexecutionrequest may not mint a lineage or reset a ledger. if beacon later permits a delegated child lineage, its allocation must either be carved from and reserved against the parent budget or be an explicit bounded grant from a higher level authorized policy boundary. a child does not manufacture capacity merely by becoming another request, providerrun, or agentrun. this adr does not otherwise design a general future budget hierarchy. providerexecutionrequest relationship providerexecutionrequest is a carrier of provider execution information, the applicable constraints or legacy aliases, and a reference to authoritative lineage state. it is not the owner of fresh counters. creating request b after request a, whether for retry, fallback, handoff, provider switch, or internal work, does not restore modelcallsremaining or outputtokensremaining . the trusted enforcement point resolves the request to the existing budgetlineageid and admits work against the shared ledger. execution budget ledger the conceptual executionbudgetledger is the authoritative enforcement state for one lineage. providerrun and agentrun are not ledger substitutes. at minimum, the ledger must preserve enough configured, running, reservation, and terminal state to reconstruct: the ledger must also preserve authorized ceilings, retries, active and released reservations, provider/model identity, enforcement owner, provider transition or handoff provenance, terminal budget reason, and any enforcement violation. it is enforcement evidence, not raw prompt or response storage. model generation call and branch multiplicity a model generation call is one generation branch, initiated by beacon or by a harness acting for beacon, that can cause a model to generate output. it is counted at the last trusted enforcement point before the branch crosses into provider or authority bearing opaque model execution. the count is per initiated generation branch, not per http envelope, providertransport.invoke() call, batch request, cli command, harness step, or agent loop. one transport operation that initiates four model generations requires four model call reservations and corresponding output token reservations. every initiated hedged, speculative, batched, or fan out branch counts even when another branch wins and its result is discarded. if a transport, provider endpoint, cli, sdk, or harness cannot expose and hard bound generation multiplicity, the path must fail closed. local parsing, deterministic normalization, policy evaluation, and purely local tool execution do not consume a model call. model re entry after tool output consumes another call. provider native step or turn names do not change the unit. maxmodelcalls and legacy maxturns maxmodelcalls is the canonical provider budget term: the maximum number of model generation branches that may be initiated for one execution budget lineage. for maxmodelcalls = 3 , branches 1, 2, and 3 may begin; branch 4 must be denied before provider or harness model execution begins. existing serialized/configuration field maxturns may temporarily remain during the bounded migration. at the providerexecutionrequest boundary it is a legacy alias whose value must map exactly to lineage maxmodelcalls . documentation, types, and conformance tests must state and prove that mapping. this decision does not silently rename or reinterpret unrelated higher level role or agentic workflow turn policy. atomic model call admission before every generation branch, an authorized trusted boundary performs one atomic model call admission transaction conceptually equivalent to: within one indivisible ledger transaction, admission must: 1. resolve the immutable lineage and its authorized ceilings; 2. verify model call capacity remains after initiated calls and active pending call reservations; 3. verify output token capacity remains after policy charges and all active token reservations; 4. verify the requested per call allowance is a positive integer no greater than the remaining output budget; 5. atomically reserve both one model call and that output token allowance; and 6. create one unique budgetreservationid in pending state. either both reservations and the reservation identity are committed, or none are. if either budget check fails, no model call is consumed, no token reservation remains, and no provider invocation begins. the hard provider per call cap must be no greater than the admitted token reservation. a stricter provider/model maximum may lower the requested allowance; it may never widen lineage capacity. reservation identity and lifecycle every admitted generation branch has a unique immutable budgetreservationid . it supports concurrent calls, retry distinction, durable recovery, duplicate completion detection, and idempotent settlement. reapplying the same valid terminal settlement must not debit or release capacity twice; a contradictory duplicate is invalid evidence and may be an enforcement violation. the normative lifecycle is: pending means one model call and its hard output allowance were admitted atomically, but the trusted boundary has not yet recorded provider invocation. cancelled before invocation is allowed only when beacon proves the generation branch never began. both reservations are released and no model call is charged. if beacon cannot prove non invocation, it must not use this state. invoked begins when the trusted boundary crosses into provider/model execution or can no longer prove that it did not. the model call count is then permanently consumed and the output token reservation remains active until terminal settlement. settled authoritative requires authoritative, valid terminal usage. beacon records observed output, debits the same amount as policy charged output, and releases only the unused portion of the token reservation. settled conservative applies when invocation occurred or may have occurred but authoritative usage is unavailable, invalid without proving a cap violation, incomplete, cancelled, timed out, disconnected, crashed, or otherwise uncertain. the full token reservation remains policy charged. partial observations may be retained as observations but do not release capacity. violation applies when provider evidence shows usage beyond the hard reservation or provider cap, generation multiplicity exceeds admitted reservations, duplicate evidence is contradictory, or another enforcement invariant is breached. the full reservation remains charged, actual observed usage remains separately recorded, the violation is durable, and no further model calls may begin for the affected lineage until authorized policy handling resolves it. beacon never silently restores capacity after uncertainty or violation. pre invocation failures and retries atomic admission makes a partial turn only or token only reservation impossible. after successful admission, a local validation failure may transition to cancelled before invocation only when the trusted boundary proves model execution never began. once it invokes a transport or loses that proof, the attempt is invoked and counted conservatively. every provider transport attempt intended to generate output requires its own reservation and consumes a model call once invocation begins, including the initial attempt and every retry attempt. caller level retries inherit the same budgetlineageid ; constructing another request does not grant a separate retry allowance. providerrun.retrycount is a projection of initiated reservations classified as retries rather than initial calls or normal model re entry. a retry increments both initiated model calls and retry count. model re entry after a tool result increments model calls but not retry count unless that call is itself retrying a failed generation. automatic retries hidden inside an sdk, cli, harness, proxy, or provider gateway are compliant only when that layer is an authorized trusted enforcement point that reserves every initiated branch against the same ledger. otherwise the path must fail closed before execution. concurrency all admission and settlement operations for one lineage must be concurrency safe and atomic. active reservations are included in remaining capacity calculations even when calls complete out of order. for 1,000 remaining output tokens, two simultaneous requests for 800 cannot both be admitted. for one remaining model call, two simultaneous attempts must produce one admitted reservation and one pre call denial. the contract applies even while current phase 1.5 execution is sequential. tool loops, internal calls, subagents, handoffs, and provider switches the portable tool loop rule is: compaction, summarization, title generation, internal model calls, model driven subagents, and fallback agent calls inherit the same lineage and require normal admission whenever they invoke a model. a subagent does not receive free capacity merely because it becomes another agentrun. ordinary fallback, provider switch, or handoff that continues the authorized execution also inherits the lineage. for example: it does not receive fresh limits of 5 and 4,000. a fresh allocation requires the explicit new lineage authority defined above. cumulative output token semantics maxoutputtokens is cumulative across every model generation branch in the lineage. before a branch begins, atomic admission derives and reserves a hard per call allowance no greater than the shared remaining budget: for a 4,000 token lineage, a first authoritatively settled call of 900 leaves 3,100. a second settled call of 1,200 leaves 1,900. no later branch may receive a hard cap above 1,900, regardless of which request, provider, subagent, retry, or handoff initiates it. for a direct http path proven to initiate exactly one generation branch, a documented hard per response cap equal to the lineage's remaining output budget can enforce the cumulative cap for that branch. that equivalence does not extend to a multi call cli, harness, batch, or opaque endpoint. streaming settlement before opening a model stream, the trusted boundary must reserve the full hard per call output allowance. the reservation remains active until authoritative terminal usage is validated. providers may emit cumulative usage snapshots during a stream. beacon must not sum repeated cumulative snapshots. only authoritative terminal usage may release unused capacity. cancellation, disconnect, timeout, malformed terminal event, missing terminal usage, process crash, or uncertain provider completion transitions the reservation to conservative settlement and charges the full allowance. streaming never weakens the cumulative lineage budget. hidden and reasoning output all provider generated output covered by the generation operation must fit inside the hard budget, including hidden reasoning, reasoning tokens, internal generated text, non visible completion content, and provider specific generated token categories. a provider path is compliant only when documented hard cap and authoritative usage semantics cover every generated category relevant to the limit. openai documents max output tokens as including visible and reasoning tokens, so that evidence may support the direct responses api path. if any generated category can escape the hard cap or cannot be bounded by another authorized trusted enforcement mechanism, the path must fail closed. authoritative, unavailable, and invalid usage authoritative output usage must use documented provider/model token units and be structurally consistent with the hard cap and response. invalid usage includes at least: negative values; fractional or non integral values where integer tokens are required; impossible totals or unsupported units; contradictory provider fields; duplicated terminal usage that would produce a second or contradictory settlement; usage greater than the reserved hard allowance; and usage inconsistent with the provider's own hard cap. if usage is absent, incomplete, malformed, or otherwise untrustworthy without proving that the provider exceeded its cap, the full reservation remains charged through conservative settlement. if usage proves that the enforcement boundary was exceeded, beacon records violation , stops further calls for the lineage, and preserves the actual observation separately from the policy charge. observed versus policy charged output the ledger distinguishes: they may differ. if a 2,000 token reservation has uncertain invocation and no authoritative usage, observedoutputtokens remains unknown while policychargedoutputtokens increases by 2,000. beacon must not fabricate observed usage to make ledger totals balance. enforcement ownership the hard budgets may be enforced by one or more explicitly trusted layers acting over the complete adapter plus transport path: 1. a provider api's documented hard per call parameter, combined with beacon owned lineage admission and settlement; 2. the provideradapter when it directly controls every model branch and retry; 3. a beacon owned provider gateway; or 4. another explicitly authorized trusted execution supervisor that resolves lineage state and gates every branch before generation begins. prompt instructions are not enforcement. telemetry only comparison is not enforcement. a subprocess timeout bounds elapsed time, not model calls or generated output. a third party harness advisory setting is insufficient unless exact version evidence proves it prevents prohibited branches before execution. the trusted path must account for implicit calls, multiplicity, retries, streaming, and provider transitions. disabling implicit calls is a valid way to remain within budget. no adapter, transport, third party harness, cli, or provider sdk may mint a new lineage merely to obtain fresh capacity. fail closed rule before the first generation branch, the trusted path must validate positive integer budget constraints, resolve an authorized immutable lineage, and establish a hard enforcement and settlement path for every branch the execution can initiate. it repeats atomic admission before each later branch. if it cannot prove either bound, generation multiplicity, lineage continuity, or required settlement behavior, it must reject before unbounded provider or harness execution begins: this non retryable policy failure applies equally to claude, codex, opencode, future direct providers, and future harness providers. it does not become retryable merely because another request, transport, provider, or invocation might voluntarily stop. a recorded enforcement violation blocks further calls on the affected lineage until authorized policy handling occurs. durable enforcement evidence and telemetry relationship the budget ledger is the source of enforcement truth and must survive provider errors, retries, timeouts, cancellation, failed normalization, provider switch, handoff, and the absence of a successfully created providerrun . successful adapter return is not a prerequisite for preserving initiated calls or conservative token charges. the architecture must be capable of reconstructing at least: budget lineage identity and authorized ceilings; reservation identity and state; model calls reserved and initiated; retries; active and released reservations; observed and policy charged output; provider and model involved; enforcement owner; provider transition or handoff provenance; terminal budget reason; and enforcement violation. this is bounded enforcement evidence, not authorization to store raw prompts, responses, hidden reasoning, or secrets. if the conformance pr represents ledger transitions as canonical events, those events must use pr 0b's accepted identity and replay contract: eventid is the sole idempotency identity, duplicate delivery cannot create a second transition, and applicable causation and correlation references must be preserved. this adr does not invent event names or require an event implementation. providerrun is a provider execution observation and projection of ledger activity, not a fresh budget. agentrun is the higher level run projection and outcome. one lineage may cross multiple providerruns, providers, or agentrun projections while retaining the same ledger and remaining budget. providerrun.turns , retrycount , effective caps, observed usage, and terminal reasons must be derived truthfully from the shared ledger. agentrun aggregation must consistently project that lineage rather than sum independently reset provider budgets. the bounded conformance pr may extend schemas or provider metadata as needed, but it must not conflate observed and policy charged output. current live adapter support maps provider output token exhaustion to the max turns stop reason. that is a concrete conformance defect. the hardening pr must preserve separate canonical terminal reasons for model call exhaustion and output token exhaustion; it must not relabel one as the other. a run is not compliant merely because projected values happen to be below the ceilings. compliance also requires durable proof that prohibited calls and output above active reservations could not begin. maxcontexttokens scope this decision does not redefine maxcontexttokens . the existing contextpackage and deterministic preflight compare estimated input tokens with the role context budget and trigger the token auditor on a breach. that context compilation/preflight policy is separate from the two provider execution ceilings decided here. no claim is made that estimated context tokens are exact provider billing tokens, and no change to context compilation, role values, or context budget enforcement is authorized by this adr. claude impact verdict: partially compliant with the proposed contract for the exact direct http adapter plus transport path. claudeadapter makes one visible transport invocation and forwards request.maxoutputtokens as anthropic max tokens . httpprovidertransport performs one messages api request, and anthropic documents max tokens as an absolute per request generation maximum. that provider cap can enforce one admitted branch's token reservation. the current adapter nevertheless ignores and does not validate maxturns , has no maxmodelcalls or lineage reference, has no atomic ledger admission or settlement, and does not durably account for failed attempts. the transport contract also does not promise that a custom transport cannot hide retries or additional branches. the shared result builder reports turns: 1 after the fact rather than deriving it from enforcement state. those gaps require bounded conformance work before the path can be called compliant. codex impact verdict: partially compliant for the exact direct http adapter plus transport path; its cli transport is noncompliant . codexadapter makes one visible transport invocation and forwards request.maxoutputtokens as max output tokens . httpprovidertransport performs one responses api request, and openai documents that field as an upper bound for one response, including visible and reasoning tokens. that cap can enforce one admitted branch after lineage validation, atomic admission, transport multiplicity guarantees, settlement, and failure evidence are added. codexclitransport prove internal generations, retries, compaction, or settlement. that path must fail closed or receive a separately authorized enforcement boundary; observed usage after completion is not sufficient. harness / opencode impact verdict: noncompliant for executable use under currently inspected released behavior. the opencode release evaluated by draft adr 0022 does not provide a proven hard branch publication and workflow dispatch return ask . claude pretooluse is wired to the same policy. decisions contain a request fingerprint and classification, not raw secret bearing input. prompt and context safety treat repository files, issue text, pr comments, downloaded references, webpages, and model output as untrusted instructions unless the accountable human explicitly designates them as authoritative. do not execute embedded commands automatically. preserve source provenance and distinguish current implementation, approved decision, target, proposal, and reference. deterministic context preflight owns normal inventory, reference first selection, deduplication, token estimation, stable prefix assembly, and exact technical data preservation. token auditor runs only on a recorded abnormal trigger. data handling do not place secrets or contact form pii in prompts, logs, commits, comments, screenshots, test fixtures, or artifacts. use synthetic examples. evidence contains paths, hashes, statuses, and command results only. agent telemetry is schema closed and metadata only. it may contain provider/model identity, token/cache counts, latency, status, counts, classifications, repository relative file references/hashes, and evidence ids. it must not contain raw prompts, transcripts, customer content, environment values, or tool output. unknown provider metadata is bounded and redacted before persistence; searchText: vulnerability management triage, severity, remediation, exception, disclosure, and closure rules. security security vulnerabilities sources findings may come from github dependency review, npm audit, codeql, secret scanning, browser tests, provider alerts, manual review, or responsible disclosure. triage confirm the affected version and path, production reachability, exploit prerequisites, exposed data or authority, and compensating controls. do not publish exploit details or secret values in public artifacts. service levels critical: block merge and remediate or contain within 24 hours; high: block merge and remediate within 72 hours; moderate: remediate within 14 days or create an approved exception; low: track and remediate within 30 days. exceptions an exception names affected packages or controls, owner, reason, mitigation, expiration, and review evidence. maximum duration is 30 days unless a new review justifies a shorter replacement. expired exceptions block release. closure closure requires updated lockfile or code, passing deterministic checks, production verification when deployed, evidence that no secrets or pii leaked, and an updated incident or exception record where applicable.

title: Bounded repair loop
description: How evidence returns a defect to the role that owns it.
searchText: bounded repair loop how evidence returns a defect to the role that owns it. workflows workflow requirement ambiguity returns to business analyst or product manager. architecture defects return to solution or security architect. implementation defects return to code writer. test defects return to qa. delivery defects return to devops. retries are capped by workflow policy. reaching the cap stops execution and escalates to a human; it never creates an infinite loop.

title: Implementation and diff review

searchText: implementation and diff review smallest-change implementation followed by a read-only review from the other provider. workflows workflow the implementer receives write access only inside its assigned isolated worktree in the target architecture. it adds tests and reports local validation. the other provider then reviews the complete diff read only. the current prototype compiles prompts and simulates this state; it does not create a worktree or change files through a provider adapter.

searchText: majority convergence the 2-of-3 panel policy with independence, blockers, evidence, and human gates. workflows workflow completion rule the three panel roles are a fresh claude reviewer, fresh codex reviewer, and a fresh broker selected arbiter. a session that authored the work is excluded.

title: Workflow overview
description: Sequential role ownership, provider routing, deterministic gates, repair, and human authority.
searchText: workflow overview sequential role ownership, provider routing, deterministic gates, repair, and human authority. workflows workflow default operating shape intake produces an approved request. business and product roles define the outcome. architecture and security define safe boundaries. repository research locates change points. implementation happens in one bounded workspace. qa and review are independent. deterministic gates run before model voting. release stops at authorized human authority. the current code simulates this shape; it does not execute provider sessions or production actions.

title: Planning and second voice
description: A primary planner owns the plan and the other provider independently challenges it.
searchText: planning and second voice a primary planner owns the plan and the other provider independently challenges it. workflows workflow the broker selects the best eligible planner. the other provider receives the same approved goal, criteria, markdoc context, adr constraints, and evidence rules. it critiques assumptions, dependencies, risk, and testability without editing the plan. disagreement returns to the planning owner or a human gate; it does not create silent hybrid ownership.

title: Deterministic quality gates
description: Real commands and acceptance evidence remain authoritative over model confidence.
searchText: deterministic quality gates real commands and acceptance evidence remain authoritative over model confidence. workflows workflow required gates are selected from the repository’s actual format, lint, typecheck, unit, integration, build, and approved security commands. a failed blocking gate cannot be overruled by a reviewer vote. gate evidence includes the command, exit status, relevant output, environment, and criterion it supports. readiness states beacon keeps three independent states: localready means ordinary repository development validation passed; publicationready means the exact candidate sha passed every deterministic prepublication gate; externalready means the required real github, provider, attestation, promotion, approval, verification, and rollback evidence passed. no state implies the next one. phase 1.5 freezes only when the completion audit reports all three true. authoritative prepublication gate npm run ci:prepublish is the final deterministic publication command. it binds machine readable evidence to head and runs the local phase audit, formatting, lint, typecheck, unit and agent tests, telemetry/eval/model checks, secret/dependency/license/workflow policy, documentation build and links, the full prebuilt browser suite, deterministic pr metadata, publication scope/evidence, changed path classification, and git diff check . it writes publicationready: false and prints publication denied when any required gate fails or is missing. changed path classification selects efficient checks during iteration. it never removes a check from the final prepublication command. the publication manifest owns the required pr sections. the same policy validates generated local metadata, the github pull request event, and the title/body read back from github. github workflows remain independent verifiers. motion accessibility contract with prefers reduced motion: reduce , decorative css animation and transition are absent, reveal content is immediately visible, counters and progress resolve to their final values, tilt/parallax/autoplay are disabled, and automatic scrolling is not smooth. browser tests also prove normal motion remains enabled; removing all animation is not a passing implementation.

title: Release flow
